notes: Personality pairs (2026-10-24): relationships that come from who the heroes are, not what they drive. Every hero who had no written tie gets at least one. Merged by tools/author_bonds_v1.py.

motifs: the one who counts the living and the one who counts the dead
two quiet women who never raise their voices

C.title: Counting
beats: After every drop, Pavise counts heads. Ketha counts wrecks. They finish at the same moment.
Two didn't. I have their names.
Then between us we have all of them.

B.title: The left and the back
beats: Pavise walks on the commander's left. Ketha walks behind everyone.
You pick them up when I fail.
You don't fail often. I notice when you do. I never tell them.

A.title: Twenty years
beats: Two cups of tea, gone cold. Neither of them drinks it. That is not the point.
Twenty years with the Armada and I never had someone to hand the ones I lost to.
Now you do. I'll carry them. You keep walking left.

C.title: Line items
beats: Solarium has a spreadsheet. Consul has built three walls that are not on it.
Spreadsheets, then sunlight. In that order.
I build when it feels owed.
Feelings are not a budget line.

B.title: Owed
beats: Solarium found a column called 'Consul: apologies'. It balances to the metal.
You were going to build them anyway. I'd rather know what they cost.
Every one of them costs more than metal.

A.title: Balanced books
beats: The pad went up in half the time. Solarium planned it; Consul built it as if someone's life depended on it. Someone's did.
First time in years something I built didn't feel like penance.

C.title: Surprises
beats: Twitcher welded a mine into Cinder Hook's bunk. Cinder Hook mined Twitcher's workbench. Both are delighted.

B.title: Shop talk
beats: They have started sharing a workbench, which the rest of the camp regards as a strategic threat.
Your welds hold. My mines go off. Think of the children.

A.title: Family firm
beats: The enemy's supply road stopped existing. Nobody saw it happen. Two Cortex deserters were laughing in a ditch.
We do. They just don't know where to send the bill.

motifs: who is loudest at handshake range

C.title: Volume
beats: Cauter's riot cannon and Kit's Belchers went off at the same wall. Nobody could hear for an hour.
Fireworks as a sentence. Mine was longer.

B.title: The scoreboard
beats: They have a chalkboard. It has two columns: 'loud' and 'louder'. They keep switching which one is theirs.
You were louder today. I'm furious.
You set fire to the chalkboard.

A.title: Duet
beats: They hit the line together. Riot first, then fire, then nothing standing.
That was the loudest thing I've ever heard.
We should do it again. Louder.

motifs: two voices doing the same math

C.title: Numbers
beats: Halq calls grid references. Verse counts missiles. From a distance it sounds like a hymn.
I count everything. Yours land where you say.

B.title: Harmony
beats: They have started finishing each other's numbers.
I never reach zero without something dying.
Then let's make the math come out even.

A.title: Zero
beats: Verse reached zero. Halq's map was empty. Neither of them said a word for a long time.
That's the first time the grid had nothing left on it.
I counted it with you. It sounded better in two voices.

motifs: three wars unpaid, collected in person

C.title: Arrears
beats: The Auditor sits down next to Grath at the fire. Grath does not move. Nobody else breathes.
Ledger with legs. Three wars, Grath.

B.title: Payment plan
beats: The Auditor walked beside Grath's Karkinos all sortie, and wrote down every enemy he held back.
Counting your payments. You've been making them for years. Nobody wrote them down.

A.title: Paid
beats: The Auditor tore a page out of its ledger and handed it to Grath.
Receipt. Three wars. Paid in full, by holding the middle.
...I don't know how to stand without the weight.
Then hold the middle for free. It looks the same from outside.

motifs: counting out loud against counting the cost

C.title: Expenditure
beats: Verse counts missiles out loud. The Auditor counts their price, also out loud.
One thousand two hundred, two thousand four hundred...

B.title: Value
beats: Every missile is a word, you said. Do you know what your words cost?
Do you know what silence costs? I counted it once. It cost us Rusk's gate.

A.title: Worth it
beats: The Auditor has stopped reading the price aloud. It just writes 'worth it' beside each of Verse's volleys.
I started trusting the count you do.

C.title: Wheels
beats: Spoke trusts nothing that walks. Stride does not walk.
We don't count shots. We count exits.

B.title: Racing
beats: A Wheelie and a Saloon raced the whole map and both claim they won.
Your manners are faster. You insulted the referee.

A.title: Every exit
beats: When the pad was overrun, every pack got out. Spoke's scouts had found the gaps; Stride had already driven through them.
I trust you now. Don't make it weird.
We'd never. Weird is a door. We just leave through it.

C.title: Big
beats: The Tzar and the Halberd park side by side. The ground complains.

B.title: Sharing
beats: They take turns on the walls now. Bro arrives, the Halberd eats what's left.
I'm not angry. I'm available. You're hungry. Works out.

A.title: Brothers
beats: Something big came at the pad. Something bigger met it, and then something hungrier.

motifs: the shrug that insults the walk

C.title: Why
beats: Brakhov burned his name off for this war. Bro is here because someone asked nicely.
Name gone. Forward heat. Why are you here?

B.title: Arriving
beats: They reached the same turret line. Brakhov walked into the fire. Bro drove around it and took it from behind.

A.title: Reasons
beats: Brakhov asked Bro, at the fire, whether he had ever had a name worth burning.
Had one. Didn't need to burn it. Nobody ever asked for it.
Nah. It's lighter. You could try it.

motifs: one grows legs, one grows sun

C.title: Crops
beats: Solarium plants solar panels in rows. The Infestor plants itself in the gaps between them.
...They are very tidy rows, at least.

B.title: Fertile
beats: The hive grew twice as fast beside the solar field. Solarium noticed, and added a row.
I can budget for warm ground.

A.title: Harvest
beats: The garden held: panels, converters and a ring of legs that would not let anything near them.
You're the best fence I've ever planted.

motifs: finishing sentences against starting new ones

C.title: Names
beats: Ketha brings back the dead by name. The Infestor makes new bodies that never had one.
Wrecks are unfinished sentences. Yours never start.
Growing isn't the same as remembering.

B.title: Counting legs
beats: Ketha has started naming the Infestor's spawn. There are a lot of them.
Everyone does. Even if they only live a minute. That one's called Brant.

A.title: Brant
beats: One of the hive's bugs came home dragging a hero's wreck back to Ketha's rez-bot.
It remembered what you told it.
Then it's a sentence after all.

C.title: Staying
beats: Stride drove through the pad four times today. Hearth has not moved in a month.
It's the only answer. Somebody has to be where you come back to.

B.title: Coming back
beats: Stride drove home through enemy fire because the lights at the pad were still on.
I could see you from across the map.

A.title: Home
beats: Stride parked next to the reactor and turned the engines off. Nobody had ever seen them do that.
For a minute. Don't tell anyone. We have a reputation.

C.title: Holding
beats: Rusk holds the gate. Warder holds the circle. They sit back to back, not talking.

B.title: The lie
beats: What was the lie? At the gate.
Told them reinforcements were coming. Held six hours on it.
No. But I'd have held either way. The lie was for them, not me.

A.title: Reinforcements
beats: Rusk's gate was failing. Warder's beamers rolled up behind it. Warder had left the circle.
The lie should come true once.

motifs: two quiet killers in the fog

C.title: Quiet
beats: Two people who never raise their voices have found each other, and the camp is uneasy about it.
The wall never saw the invoice.
We're the same thing at different distances.

B.title: Leaving
beats: You leave before they know you were there.
So do you. You just leave a bill.
Someone has to pay for the quiet.

A.title: Nothing heard
beats: An entire enemy front lost its commanders and its walls on the same night. Nobody heard a thing.

motifs: two captains, one who never shouts
orders that walk and orders that wait

C.title: Volume
beats: Quill gives orders like artillery. Pavise gives them like weather reports.
Orders walk on treads. They don't ask twice.
They shouldn't need to. If you have to shout, you've already lost them.

B.title: Listening
beats: Quill tried giving a quiet order. The Bulls followed it faster.
People lean in to hear you when you're quiet. They lean back when you shout.

A.title: Succession
beats: Pavise was down. Quill held the line without raising his voice once.
I heard you on the radio. You sounded like me.
I had a good teacher. Don't you dare die before I'm better at it.

motifs: the saint's garden and the welder's surprises

C.title: Sacred ground
beats: Twitcher welded a booby trap into Sister Lumen's geothermal vent. She found it during prayers.
Tithe the grid. Not the grid's plumbing.

B.title: Confession
beats: Is there a saint of mischief?
You'd have to stop booby-trapping the altar.

A.title: Blessed traps
beats: Raiders came for Lumen's Pulsar. Twitcher's traps were all around it. She had let him plant them.
Did you just bless my mines?
Once. Don't make me regret it.

motifs: the spare king and the man who'll follow anyone

C.title: Your Majesty
beats: Bro saluted Mask. Mask was so surprised he saluted back.

B.title: Royal escort
beats: The Tzar has started following Mask around the battlefield, flattening anything that threatens the Pawns.
You don't have to protect me. I'm a decoy.
Decoys need protecting most. Everybody's aiming at you.

A.title: Crowned
beats: Sixteen Pawns, a Tzar and a decoy commander walked into the enemy's camp like a parade.
Told you. Belief's available. You just had to ask.

C.title: Parking
beats: Odessa's Telchines came up the ford and found six Cutlasses floating in it.
Fords are doors. You're parked in my doorway.
Lands where nobody parks. Somebody does now.

B.title: Shared water
beats: You could cross under us. We float.
I don't cross under things. I own the hinge.
Then we'll own the sky over your hinge. Deal?

A.title: Flood door
beats: The water rose over the ford. Odessa held it from below; Gale held it from above. The enemy never found a way across.
